# Obviously — Style Reference

> Colored index tabs clipped into a white lab notebook. Epilogue at weight 500 tightened to -0.04em, a white canvas over a periwinkle wash, single-stroke line drawings, and one cobalt button as the action.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Obviously speaks a color-coded-notebook product language. A #ffffff canvas carries the hero, and a full-bleed #f3f5fc periwinkle wash holds white #ffffff feature cards, so surfaces are separated by tone. The chromatic budget is four flat hues used as a category code: cobalt #267dff, mint #00d085, amethyst #9867ff and sunbeam #f4e82f. Each product capability owns one of them, and that hue appears only as a whole-tile fill, a 4px tag or an illustration panel. Cobalt alone doubles as the action fill. Typography runs on a single family, Epilogue. Headlines are set at weight 500 from 24px to 64px, tracked at a constant -0.04em, on a near-Perfect-Fourth ladder of 24, 32, 48 and 64px. Hierarchy comes from size and that tight tracking, not from bold. Shapes are soft: 10px cards and CTAs, 4px tags and nav buttons, and no shadows on content. The result reads as a filing system with labeled tabs rather than a gradient-lit AI showroom.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page body, feature-card fill on the wash, secondary-button fill, and text on colored tiles (21 background uses, 29 text uses) — the neutral the four category hues sit against. |
| Mist Wash | `#f3f5fc` | `--color-mist-wash` | Full-bleed feature band, the video card and the page band behind white cards — a blue-tinted step that replaces shadows as the separator between canvas and card. |
| Jet Ink | `#262626` | `--color-jet-ink` | Every h1, h2 and h3 on white, plus inactive nav links (36 uses) — a softened black that keeps 64px medium headlines from reading as harsh. |
| Graphite Body | `#3e343f` | `--color-graphite-body` | Card paragraphs, the secondary-button label and text on sunbeam tags (34 uses) — a plum-tinted graphite that warms long-form copy beside the cool blues. |
| Graphite Caption | `#3e343f80` | `--color-graphite-caption` | Muted supporting lines and secondary metadata (9 uses) — Graphite Body at 50% alpha, so the hue family stays intact as text recedes. |
| Fog Border | `#ebebeb` | `--color-fog-border` | The 1px border on the Sign in and Learn More buttons and the rare dividers — the only opaque hairline in the system. Do not use it to outline cards. |
| Frosted Hairline | `#ebebeb26` | `--color-frosted-hairline` | The 1px outline on the Learn more ghost buttons inside colored tiles (4 uses) — 15% alpha lets the tile hue show through the border. |
| Signal Cobalt | `#267dff` | `--color-signal-cobalt` | Get Started fill, active nav link, Classification tile and Model Monitoring tag (7 fills) — both a category color and the sole action color. |
| Mint Code | `#00d085` | `--color-mint-code` | Regression tile, Model Deployment tag and illustration panels — a category marker only. Do not promote it to a CTA, because white text on it falls below 2.5:1. |
| Amethyst Code | `#9867ff` | `--color-amethyst-code` | Time Series tile, Expert Support tag and the offset frame shadow on the video mockup — the third category hue and the only colored shadow. |
| Sunbeam Code | `#f4e82f` | `--color-sunbeam-code` | Model Building and Integration tags, plus the prediction-quality illustration panel — the one light hue, so it always takes Graphite Body text and never white. |
| Ember Banner | `#dc2626` | `--color-ember-banner` | The full-width archive notice above the nav and nothing else — a status color. Do not reuse it for errors in product UI or for decoration. |
| Steel Consent | `#1863dc` | `--color-steel-consent` | Consent-manager buttons, links and 2px borders (5 fills, 6 borders) — a third-party widget color. Keep it out of brand components. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Epilogue — the single family covering display headlines, nav, buttons and body copy · `--font-epilogue`

- **Substitute:** Epilogue itself is free on Google Fonts, so use it at the same weights. If you need a fallback, DM Sans at 500 for headlines and 400 for body comes close. Manrope also works at 600 for headlines and 400 for body, because Manrope draws lighter than its nominal weight. Epilogue 500 renders slightly heavier than a typical grotesk 500, so do not drop a substitute to 400 for headlines or it will look thin.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14px, 15px, 16px, 18px, 20px, 24px, 32px, 40px, 44px, 48px, 64px
- **Line height:** 1.0–1.04 for display and headings, 1.17 at 24px, 1.33–1.5 for body, 1.71 for 14px consent copy
- **Letter spacing:**
  - -2.56px at 64px, -1.92px at 48px, -1.6px at 40px, -1.28px at 32px and -0.96px at 24px (a constant -0.04em)
  - -0.16px on 16px weight-700 button labels (-0.01em)
  - normal everywhere else
- **Role:** Weight 500 at display sizes is the signature. The headlines are large but never shout, against the SaaS convention of 700 bold heroes. Every heading shares the same -0.04em tracking, which gives the page one tight, engineered texture from 24px to 64px. The heading ladder of 24, 32, 48 and 64px steps by about 1.333, a Perfect Fourth. Using one family means hierarchy depends on size, tracking and the 400/500/600/700 weight split rather than a font pairing: 600 for nav, 700 for button labels, 400 for reading.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Epilogue | 400 | 12px | 1.58 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Epilogue | 400 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Epilogue | 400 | 15px | 1.33 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Epilogue | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Epilogue | 400 | 20px | 1.35 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Epilogue | 500 | 24px | 1.17 | -0.96px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Epilogue | 500 | 32px | 1.03 | -1.28px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Epilogue | 500 | 40px | 1.0 | -1.6px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Epilogue | 500 | 48px | 1.0 | -1.92px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Epilogue | 500 | 64px | 1.04 | -2.56px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Assign each capability exactly one of #267dff, #00d085, #9867ff or #f4e82f, and repeat that hue on its tag, tile and illustration panel — the color code works only if the mapping holds across the page.
- Set every heading from 24px to 64px at weight 500 with -0.04em tracking (-2.56px at 64px) — the uniform tight tracking is the typographic signature.
- Separate cards from the page with tone: #ffffff cards on a #f3f5fc band, with no shadow — tonal layering keeps the page flat and diagrammatic.
- Use 10px radius on content cards and CTAs, and 4px on tags, nav buttons and category tiles — the two-step radius tells containers apart from labels.
- Set text on #f4e82f in #3e343f and text on the other three hues in #ffffff — the light hue is the only one that inverts.
- Lay out feature grids as 540px columns with a 30px gap inside the 1110px container — the 30px gutter is the most frequent spacing value (44 uses).
- Keep one #267dff filled button per viewport, labeled in Epilogue 16px at weight 700 — rationed action color keeps cobalt meaningful as both category and CTA.

### Don't

- Don't bold headlines to 700 at 48px or 64px — weight 500 is what makes the large sizes quiet, and bold turns the notebook into a billboard.
- Don't add a fifth saturated hue (a coral or teal accent) for a new feature — the four-color category code is non-negotiable, and a fifth tab breaks the index.
- Never put white text on #f4e82f — contrast drops below 1.3:1 and the tag becomes unreadable.
- Don't give feature cards a soft drop shadow such as 0px 4px 12px — elevation here comes from the #f3f5fc to #ffffff surface shift, and blur makes the page muddy.
- Don't use #00d085 as a button fill — white labels on mint fall below 2.5:1, and the hue loses its job as a category marker.
- Don't reuse #1863dc or the 2px consent radius in brand UI — those belong to the cookie vendor and split the blue into two competing values.
- Never loosen heading tracking to 0px at 48px — Epilogue opens up visibly, and the engineered density of the -1.92px setting is lost.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- section wash: #f3f5fc (Mist Wash)
- heading text: #262626 (Jet Ink)
- body text: #3e343f (Graphite Body)
- hairline: #ebebeb (Fog Border)
- category hues: #00d085 (Mint Code), #9867ff (Amethyst Code), #f4e82f (Sunbeam Code)
- primary action: #267dff (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Saturated hues appear in data only as solid fills on small markers, such as 24px circular class badges, short bars inside an illustration panel or a tag chip. Numbers and labels stay in #262626 and #3e343f on #ffffff, and a full chart area or background is not flooded with a category hue.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button labeled "Try for free". Use a #267dff background, #ffffff text and a 1px solid #267dff border, with 10px border-radius and 12px 30px padding. Set the label in Epilogue 16px at weight 700, line-height 1.5, letter-spacing -0.16px. Add no box-shadow. On hover, keep the fill and shift nothing larger than a 2px translate. Place it 40px below the card's body copy.

2. Build the navigation bar on #ffffff with no border or shadow, a 1110px max-width and position relative (not sticky). Put the logo on the left. Center links "Software", "Service", "Pricing", "Use Cases", "Success Stories ▾" and "Resources ▾" in Epilogue 16px at weight 600, #262626, with a 30px gap between them, and make the active link #267dff. On the right, add "Sign in": #ffffff fill, #3e343f text, 1px solid #ebebeb border, 4px radius, padding 8px 45px 6px. Next to it, 30px away, add "Get Started": #267dff fill, #ffffff text, 1px solid #267dff border, 4px radius, the same padding and Epilogue 16px weight 600.

3. Build a three-column category section inside a 1110px container with a 30px gap. Make each tile a solid fill with 4px radius, 40px padding, center-aligned content and no shadow: #267dff for "Classification", #00d085 for "Regression" and #9867ff for "Time Series". Stack these items vertically:
   - a 24px white single-stroke line icon
   - a 16px gap
   - the h3 in Epilogue 24px at weight 500, line-height 1.17, letter-spacing -0.96px, #ffffff
   - 14px weight-400 #ffffff copy at line-height 1.43
   - a 40px gap
   - a ghost button with transparent fill, 1px solid #ebebeb26 border, 10px radius, 12px 30px padding and Epilogue 16px weight 600 #ffffff
   - a flat line illustration bleeding to the bottom edge

4. Build a feature card grid on a full-bleed #f3f5fc band with 102px top and bottom padding. Each card is #ffffff with 10px radius, 40px padding, and no border or shadow, and cards sit in a two-column grid of 540px columns with a 30px gap. Inside each card, add these in order:
   - a tag with 4px radius, 5px 8px 2px padding and Epilogue 14px weight 400 (fill #00d085 with #ffffff text, or #f4e82f with #3e343f text)
   - an h3 in Epilogue 32px at weight 500, line-height 1.03, letter-spacing -1.28px, #262626, 24px below the tag
   - body copy in 14px #3e343f at line-height 1.43, 16px below the h3
   - above the text, an illustration panel filled with the same hue as the tag, 6px radius, containing a #ffffff mockup outlined with 1px #262626

## Components

### Archive Banner — Ember Status Strip

**Role:** Site-wide archival notice above navigation

A deliberate red interruption. The banner fills the full width with Ember Banner #dc2626, sets white #ffffff text in Epilogue 14px at weight 400, has 0px radius and 12px vertical padding, and centers a small dark badge filled with #1a1a1a (banner-internal, not a system token). That badge carries 4px radius, 8px 20px 6px padding and white 14px weight-500 text. This is the system outlier: the only red and the only full-bleed saturated strip. It is allowed because it announces a status change, not brand expression.

### Navigation Bar

**Role:** Logo, centered links, paired actions

A flat white header row. It sits on Paper Canvas #ffffff with no border or shadow and scrolls away rather than sticking (position relative, 42px inner row). The logo is left, the links are centered in Epilogue 16px weight 600 Jet Ink #262626 with the active link in Signal Cobalt #267dff, and dropdown carets mark Success Stories and Resources. Two 4px-radius buttons sit right, 30px apart. The weight-600 links make the nav quieter than the 700 buttons beside it, so attention lands on Get Started.

### Filled Button — Cobalt (Primary)

**Role:** Get Started, Try for free

The single action color. Fill is Signal Cobalt #267dff with white #ffffff text and a 1px #267dff border. Radius is 10px in the hero and in cards, and padding is 12px 30px. Label type is Epilogue 16px at weight 700 with -0.16px tracking, and there is no shadow. The nav instance tightens to 4px radius and 8px 45px 6px padding at a 40px height. Use one per viewport — because cobalt is also a category hue, a second filled button blurs the line between label and action.

### Outlined Button — Fog (Secondary)

**Role:** Sign in, Learn More

The quiet counterpart. Fill is Paper Canvas #ffffff, text is Graphite Body #3e343f, and the border is a 1px Fog Border #ebebeb hairline. It matches the primary in geometry: 10px radius in the hero, 4px with 8px 45px 6px padding in the nav, and Epilogue 16px at weight 600–700. There is no shadow. The near-invisible #ebebeb border makes this read as a text link with a footprint rather than a competing button.

### Ghost Button on Color — Frosted Hairline

**Role:** Learn more inside category tiles

A translucent outline. The fill is transparent over the tile hue, the text is white #ffffff in Epilogue 16px at weight 600, and the border is 1px Frosted Hairline #ebebeb26. Radius is 10px, padding is 12px 30px, and the button is centered. Because the 15% alpha border lets cobalt, mint or amethyst show through, one component works on all three tiles without per-color variants.

### Category Tile — Colored (Classification, Regression, Time Series)

**Role:** Color-coded capability entry point

Whole-surface hue blocks. The fill is Signal Cobalt #267dff, Mint Code #00d085 or Amethyst Code #9867ff, with 4px radius, 40px padding, no border and no shadow. Content is centered: a 24px white line icon, a white h3 in Epilogue 24px at weight 500 with -0.96px tracking, white 14px weight-400 copy, a ghost button, and an illustration bleeding to the bottom edge. Tiles run in three equal columns with a 30px gap. The tighter 4px radius against the 10px content cards marks these as tabs, not containers.

### Feature Card — White on Wash

**Role:** Main content card for capabilities

The workhorse container. Fill is Paper Canvas #ffffff on a Mist Wash #f3f5fc band, with 10px radius, 40px padding, no border and no shadow. Copy is Graphite Body #3e343f in Epilogue 14px at 1.43. The order inside is: a 4px category tag, an h2/h3 at 48px or 32px weight 500 in Jet Ink #262626, body copy, then a colored illustration panel. One card spans the full 1110px as a split layout, and the rest form a two-column grid of 540px cards with a 30px gap. Tonal contrast does the lifting that shadows do elsewhere.

### Category Tag

**Role:** Label linking card to hue

A small hue chip. It has 4px radius and 5px 8px 2px padding, with Epilogue 14px weight-400 text at 1.43. The fill is one of the four category hues. White text sits on cobalt, mint and amethyst, and Graphite Body #3e343f text sits on Sunbeam Code #f4e82f. The asymmetric padding optically centers Epilogue's low-sitting baseline. The tag is the bridge between the color code and the white cards, carrying the hue into otherwise neutral content.

### Illustration Panel — Colored Inset

**Role:** Product mockup inside cards

A hue-filled stage. Inside a feature card, the panel uses one category fill (sunbeam, mint, cobalt or amethyst) with 6px radius and no shadow. It holds a white #ffffff UI mockup outlined in a 1px Jet Ink #262626 stroke and decorated with 1px grid textures, small circles and tilted squares. The mockup's hue matches the card's tag. This turns product screenshots into diagrams: precise outlines and flat fills read as a schematic rather than a photograph.

### Video Card — Mist Wash

**Role:** Demo video with headline

The tinted feature. Fill is Mist Wash #f3f5fc with 10px radius, 40px padding, no border and a 1110px width. Copy is an h2 in Epilogue 40px at weight 500 with -1.6px tracking, plus 14px Graphite Body #3e343f text. The video mockup on the left carries the system's only content shadow, a hard 1px 1px 0px 2px offset in Amethyst Code #9867ff. That shadow reads as a printed misregistration, not depth.

### Logo Row — Grayscale Proof

**Role:** Customer trust strip under hero

A muted credibility band. Five customer marks are rendered in light gray, estimated #d0d5d2 (decorative, not a system token), on Paper Canvas #ffffff. **Role:** Cookie banner and preferences modal

An imported widget. Buttons use Steel Consent #1863dc with a 2px border, 2px radius and 8px 30px padding, and labels are Epilogue 14px at weight 500. ## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Assign each capability exactly one of #267dff, #00d085, #9867ff or #f4e82f, and repeat that hue on its tag, tile and illustration panel — the color code works only if the mapping holds across the page.
- Set every heading from 24px to 64px at weight 500 with -0.04em tracking (-2.56px at 64px) — the uniform tight tracking is the typographic signature.
- Separate cards from the page with tone: #ffffff cards on a #f3f5fc band, with no shadow — tonal layering keeps the page flat and diagrammatic.
- Use 10px radius on content cards and CTAs, and 4px on tags, nav buttons and category tiles — the two-step radius tells containers apart from labels.
- Set text on #f4e82f in #3e343f and text on the other three hues in #ffffff — the light hue is the only one that inverts.
- Lay out feature grids as 540px columns with a 30px gap inside the 1110px container — the 30px gutter is the most frequent spacing value (44 uses).
- Keep one #267dff filled button per viewport, labeled in Epilogue 16px at weight 700 — rationed action color keeps cobalt meaningful as both category and CTA.

### Don't

- Don't bold headlines to 700 at 48px or 64px — weight 500 is what makes the large sizes quiet, and bold turns the notebook into a billboard.
- Don't add a fifth saturated hue (a coral or teal accent) for a new feature — the four-color category code is non-negotiable, and a fifth tab breaks the index.
- Never put white text on #f4e82f — contrast drops below 1.3:1 and the tag becomes unreadable.
- Don't give feature cards a soft drop shadow such as 0px 4px 12px — elevation here comes from the #f3f5fc to #ffffff surface shift, and blur makes the page muddy.
- Don't use #00d085 as a button fill — white labels on mint fall below 2.5:1, and the hue loses its job as a category marker.
- Don't reuse #1863dc or the 2px consent radius in brand UI — those belong to the cookie vendor and split the blue into two competing values.
- Never loosen heading tracking to 0px at 48px — Epilogue opens up visibly, and the engineered density of the -1.92px setting is lost.

## Imagery

There is no photography. Every visual is custom vector illustration in a consistent technical-diagram style. Mockups are drawn as white #ffffff panels with 1px #262626 outlines. They are dressed with grid textures, small hollow circles, tilted squares in category hues and dotted connector lines, and they sit on flat category-colored panels with 6px radius and no shadow. A few illustrations include a character (the Classification tile's analyst) drawn in the same monoline stroke with flat fills. Icons are 24px single-stroke line icons in white on colored tiles. The hero is an exploded diagram of a data pipeline: spreadsheet grid, pipes and a "Predicting: Conversion" readout, in black line work with cobalt accents. There are no gradients, glows or orbs, so color is always a flat category token. The narrative is that AI is drawn as a legible, labeled machine rather than a mysterious glowing brain.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1110px centered container on a 1920px canvas, and sections are separated by 102px. The page opens with the 0px-radius Ember Banner, then a non-sticky, transparent-on-white nav: logo left, four links plus two dropdowns centered, Sign in and Get Started right. The hero is centered and stacked: a line-art pipeline diagram, a 64px weight-500 headline in a 790px measure, a 20px subline, two buttons side by side with a 16px gap, then a five-logo grayscale row. The sections that follow alternate white and the #f3f5fc wash: a wash video card, a white "What's possible?" section with three category tiles in a three-column grid, then a full-bleed wash band of white feature cards (one full-width split card, then a two-column grid with a 30px gutter). The footer was not captured. Build it as a plain white multi-column link grid on 14px type. On 375px phones, drop display to 40px, use 56px section gaps and 24px card padding, and stack all grids to one column. Density: comfortable.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- section wash: #f3f5fc (Mist Wash)
- heading text: #262626 (Jet Ink)
- body text: #3e343f (Graphite Body)
- hairline: #ebebeb (Fog Border)
- category hues: #00d085 (Mint Code), #9867ff (Amethyst Code), #f4e82f (Sunbeam Code)
- primary action: #267dff (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Saturated hues appear in data only as solid fills on small markers, such as 24px circular class badges, short bars inside an illustration panel or a tag chip. Numbers and labels stay in #262626 and #3e343f on #ffffff, and a full chart area or background is not flooded with a category hue.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button labeled "Try for free". Use a #267dff background, #ffffff text and a 1px solid #267dff border, with 10px border-radius and 12px 30px padding. Set the label in Epilogue 16px at weight 700, line-height 1.5, letter-spacing -0.16px. Add no box-shadow. On hover, keep the fill and shift nothing larger than a 2px translate. Place it 40px below the card's body copy.

2. Build the navigation bar on #ffffff with no border or shadow, a 1110px max-width and position relative (not sticky). Put the logo on the left. Center links "Software", "Service", "Pricing", "Use Cases", "Success Stories ▾" and "Resources ▾" in Epilogue 16px at weight 600, #262626, with a 30px gap between them, and make the active link #267dff. On the right, add "Sign in": #ffffff fill, #3e343f text, 1px solid #ebebeb border, 4px radius, padding 8px 45px 6px. Next to it, 30px away, add "Get Started": #267dff fill, #ffffff text, 1px solid #267dff border, 4px radius, the same padding and Epilogue 16px weight 600.

3. Build a three-column category section inside a 1110px container with a 30px gap. Make each tile a solid fill with 4px radius, 40px padding, center-aligned content and no shadow: #267dff for "Classification", #00d085 for "Regression" and #9867ff for "Time Series". Stack these items vertically:
   - a 24px white single-stroke line icon
   - a 16px gap
   - the h3 in Epilogue 24px at weight 500, line-height 1.17, letter-spacing -0.96px, #ffffff
   - 14px weight-400 #ffffff copy at line-height 1.43
   - a 40px gap
   - a ghost button with transparent fill, 1px solid #ebebeb26 border, 10px radius, 12px 30px padding and Epilogue 16px weight 600 #ffffff
   - a flat line illustration bleeding to the bottom edge

4. Build a feature card grid on a full-bleed #f3f5fc band with 102px top and bottom padding. Each card is #ffffff with 10px radius, 40px padding, and no border or shadow, and cards sit in a two-column grid of 540px columns with a 30px gap. Inside each card, add these in order:
   - a tag with 4px radius, 5px 8px 2px padding and Epilogue 14px weight 400 (fill #00d085 with #ffffff text, or #f4e82f with #3e343f text)
   - an h3 in Epilogue 32px at weight 500, line-height 1.03, letter-spacing -1.28px, #262626, 24px below the tag
   - body copy in 14px #3e343f at line-height 1.43, 16px below the h3
   - above the text, an illustration panel filled with the same hue as the tag, 6px radius, containing a #ffffff mockup outlined with 1px #262626

## Category Color Discipline

The page's governing rule is that the four hues #267dff, #00d085, #9867ff and #f4e82f are labels, not decoration. Each capability owns one hue, and that hue travels from its tag to its tile to its illustration panel. The system breaks the moment a hue is used for mood, such as a mint section background, a sunbeam gradient behind the hero or an amethyst headline. Once color decorates, it stops meaning "this belongs to Model Deployment." A fifth hue breaks it as well, because readers can hold a four-tab index more easily than a seven-color palette. To add a capability, assign it an existing hue and pair it with a distinct icon, or accept a sibling of a current hue. Never mint a new color for marketing emphasis. Neutral surfaces (#ffffff, #f3f5fc) carry everything that is not a category.

## Tight Medium Display

Epilogue at weight 500 with a uniform -0.04em tracking, from 24px to 64px, is the typographic thesis: the headlines are large and quiet. The convention in AI SaaS is 700 bold heroes at default tracking, which reads as urgency. This system instead gets authority from size and density, 64px set at 1.04 line-height so the lines nearly touch. Three changes break it: raising headings to 700, loosening tracking to 0px, or opening line-height past 1.2, since each brings back a generic-landing-page texture. To extend the scale, compute any new step as size × -0.04 for tracking (a 56px heading gets -2.24px), keep weight 500, and hold line-height between 1.0 and 1.17. Reserve weight 700 for 16px button labels and weight 600 for nav, so bold stays a UI signal, not a headline voice.
